closures.detail:
Extends clam, mussel, and oyster harvest at Belfair State Park, opens clam, mussel and oyster harvest at Duckabush Tidelands and Triton Cove Tidelands, and extends oyster harvest at Point Whitney Tidelands and Point Whitney Lagoon; opens and modifies other previously announced changes to public shellfish beaches in marine areas 9 and 12.
Marine Area 9 (Admiralty Inlet): All public beaches within Port Gamble Bay south of a line drawn from Teekalet Point (Port Gamble) to Point Julia: closed until further notice. All public beaches from the northern edge of the mouth Mats Mats Bay to Paradise Bay, including Mats Mats Bay and Port Ludlow Bay: closed until further notice. Marine Area 12 (Hood Canal): All public beaches south of a line drawn from Triton Head to Tekiu Point and west of a line extending from Sisters Point due south to 47.34970, -123.04196 on the southern shore of Hood Canal: Closed to harvest. Public beaches north of a line drawn from Triton Head to Tekiu Point and east of line extending from Sisters Point due south to 47.34970, -123.04196 on the southern shore of Hood Canal: Follow seasons listed on WDFW public beach pages, searchable using the WDFW Find a Beach tool or the Washington Shellfish Safety Map . Belfair State Park: Open to clam, mussel, and oyster harvest through Oct. 31. Duckabush: Open to clam, mussel, and oyster harvest until further notice. Point Whitney Tidelands and Point Whitney Lagoon: Open to oyster harvest through Oct. 31. Triton Cove Tidelands: Open to clam and mussel harvest through Oct. 31.
closures.title: Marine Area 9 (Admiralty Inlet), Marine Area 12 (Hood Canal) shellfish beaches update - Oct. 14, 2026, until further notice.

closures.detail:
Opens a portion of the Cascade River to fishing seven days per week. Maintains previously announced bait prohibitions, single-point barbless hooks requirement for salmon on Cascade and Skagit rivers, and a reduced daily limit of two coho on the upper Skagit River. Updates temporary fishing closures scheduled for tribal fisheries on Skagit River.
Cascade River from the mouth to the Rockport-Cascade Road Bridge: Salmon open daily. Salmon daily limit is four coho. Minimum size is 12 inches. Release all salmon other than coho. Bait is prohibited and single-point barbless hooks are required for salmon. Gamefish open daily. Skagit River from the mouth to the Gilligan Creek east of Sedro-Woolley: Salmon daily limit is two coho. Minimum size is 12 inches. Release all salmon other than coho. Bait is prohibited and single-point barbless hooks are required for salmon. Skagit River from Gilligan Creek to the Baker River: Oct. 15: Closed to fishing for all species. Oct. 16–18: Salmon daily limit is two coho. Minimum size is 12 inches. Release all salmon other than coho. Bait is prohibited and single-point barbless hooks are required for salmon. Oct. 19–21: Closed to fishing for all species. Oct. 22–31: Salmon daily limit is two coho. Minimum size is 12 inches. Release all salmon other than coho. Bait is prohibited and single-point barbless hooks are required for salmon. Skagit River from the Baker River to the Marblemount Bridge (Cascade River Road): Salmon daily limit is two coho. Minimum size is 12 inches. Release all salmon other than coho. Bait is prohibited and single-point barbless hooks are required for salmon.
closures.title: Cascade River to open seven days per week to fishing, and temporary closure implemented in a portion of the Skagit River - Immediately through Oct. 31, 2026.
